newsitem.title: USA: Food aid undermined wheat-for-zinc barter -- Cargill.
newsitem.headline: Food aid undermined wheat-for-zinc barter -- Cargill.

text.p: A wheat-for-zinc barter with North Korea foundered because food aid was donated and Pyongyang wanted to use the zinc elsewhere, Cargill Inc chairman Ernie Micek said Thursday.
Micek told reporters Cargill still hoped to sell grain to North Korea, saying, "As far as we are concerned, the door is open."

Cargill received permission early this year to sell up to 500,000 tonnes of food grains to North Korea. A barter of 20,000 tonnes of wheat for 5,000 tonnes of zinc was reached in April but fell apart in early June, just before delivery.

"I think they did that because they received considerable free aid from a number of countries and aid groups around the world and they decided the limited barter materials that they had, in this case zinc, they wanted to use in some other means," Micek said.
Traders in Asia suggested at the time that North Korea, due to poor conditions, might not have had enough zinc on hand or decided to sell metal directly to reap attractive prices.

Asked about the potential for future barters, perhaps with other metals, Micek said "the number of commodities they have available for barter is very limited" because North Korea was not in a position to deliver sizable quantities.
